scope: Gameplay-cell to CellGFX presentation representations, scene-world and layer membership, per-entity transforms and visibility, model and creature content, effect instances, draw-list assembly, render submission, and presentation lifetime for the main cell mode. The boundary preserves gameplay identity, world/layer membership, and ordering; model-world traversal, render-queue construction, and RenderWare or D3D submission are replaceable presentation infrastructure.

boundaries.boundary: Gameplay cell to per-cell presentation handle allocation and reverse association
boundaries.gameplay_caller: App::cCellModeStrategy::OnEnter calls the cell presentation staging path; FUN_00e78c00 is the confirmed caller of unnamed FUN_00e6d8f0; the staged path is entered by cell-population helpers for ordinary cells and many static or periscope-shaded cells.

outputs: model, animated-creature, and structure presentation links

CellGFXObjectData::mCellIndex provides the reverse association
the entity's model-world and animation state are populated
boundaries.lifetime: The gameplay cell owns the identity and index field; the separately allocated CellGFXObjectData is a replaceable presentation representation and can be rebuilt, detached, or released while gameplay identity remains in the cell pool.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The recovered allocator path does not visibly guard a null pool allocation before dereferencing the returned entry, so presentation-pool exhaustion is inferred to be a fatal invariant violation rather than a gameplay-visible recoverable state.

StartDisplay activates the CellGFX display before the scene is rendered

boundaries.modern_abstraction: IEntityPresentationRegistry allocates stable handles, attaches an IEntityView, and rebuilds or detaches the view without changing the owning gameplay entity.

boundaries.boundary: Per-cell scene membership removal and presentation-component release

boundaries.lifetime: Removal is inverse to the presentation allocation but is not destruction of the gameplay cell. The boolean cleanup selector distinguishes component release from a less eager helper path, after which the presentation pool slot may be reused independently.
boundaries.failure_semantics: A missing mGFXObjectIndex value is treated as an already-detached presentation. The recovered path does not expose a recoverable model or effect release failure; repeated invalidation is expected to be safe, while partially populated representations are tolerated by per-component pointer checks.

boundaries.failure_semantics: Initialize records a failed status after several world or layer construction failures, but a normal return can still leave an incomplete scene graph. The scene contract is therefore tolerant at mode level but not a recoverable gameplay error.

boundaries.boundary: Entity-local visual effect and particle attachment

boundaries.failure_semantics: Invalid presentation handles, parent effect failures, and missing effect worlds are logged and return failure rather than failing the gameplay cell. Cleanup is pointer-checked and a failed effect creation does not create a visible instance.

boundaries.failure_semantics: StartDisplay returns true and records a status even when a sub-service activation fails; the caller treats activation as best-effort scene setup. Shutdown is guarded by pointer checks so missing services do not block mode exit.

boundaries.boundary: Model-world draw-list assembly and renderer submission
boundaries.gameplay_caller: No direct gameplay caller is proven; CellGFX layer registration, per-cell SetInWorld membership, transforms, animation, materials, LOD, and visibility are the upstream gameplay-to-presentation inputs consumed by the Graphics and renderer update path.
parameters: registered layer list and layer ordering
render groups, render-set information, materials, LOD, and effects parameters
camera, frustum, lighting, and target state
outputs: backend render state changes and indexed draw calls
state_changed: temporary or persistent draw-list membership is updated
render groups and render-set information are consumed
renderer layer queues and backend render state are populated
GPU-visible frame output is produced
boundaries.lifetime: Scene membership and layer registration are stage-scoped; draw lists and backend queues are normally frame-scoped or rebuilt from presentation state. They are not gameplay state and need not be persisted by OpenSpore.
boundaries.failure_semantics: Inactive or absent model-world membership makes an entity non-renderable. Layer, transform, material, and effect failures affect visibility or appearance but must not change gameplay ownership; RenderWare-specific allocation and draw errors are backend failures behind the renderer abstraction.
timing_order: CellGFX registers the scene layers and populates model membership
gameplay and presentation updates synchronize transforms, animation, materials, LOD, and visibility
the renderer traverses the layer graph and builds model draw lists
render jobs are ordered and submitted through Render/SubRender
RenderWare and D3D emit the final frame
boundaries.openspore_concept: Gameplay-visible semantics stop at the ordered set of visible renderable components, world/layer membership, transform, and material identity; draw-list buckets, sort keys, batch encoding, and GPU submission are replaceable renderer internals.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: ISceneRenderer snapshots renderable components, computes a per-pass draw list, and submits render passes through a backend adapter without exposing RenderWare internals.

boundaries.gameplay_caller: App::cCellModeStrategy::OnExit shuts down CellGFX; App::cCellModeStrategy::Dispose destroys it; direct constructor/destructor call sites provide the final lifetime edge.
parameters: cCellGFX-owned model worlds, effects worlds, layers, preloaded resources, and presentation pool

boundaries.lifetime: This is the terminal presentation lifetime for the main cell mode. It is ordered after gameplay cell detachment/transition work and before the mode object is released; it must not destroy gameplay systems or shared global services that outlive the mode.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The recovered teardown path uses per-pointer checks and best-effort component release, allowing incomplete initialization to be torn down. A failure to release one presentation component must not prevent the remaining layer, world, and pool cleanup.
timing_order: OnExit invokes the scene/service shutdown helper
cell presentation representations are detached and effects are stopped
layers are unregistered and worlds are disposed
FUN_00e64090 releases the cCellGFX object and its presentation pool
Dispose completes and the mode no longer owns scene presentation
boundaries.openspore_concept: A presentation stage owns all scene-local render resources and is destroyed independently from gameplay entities and global renderer services.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: ISceneStage.shutdown performs idempotent layer unregistration, view detachment, effect shutdown, and backend resource release before the stage handle is dropped.
